entries.source: SDK 26.2, MPMusicPlayerController.h, - (void)prepareToPlayWithCompletionHandler:(void (^)(NSError *_Nullable error))completionHandler MP_API(ios(10.1), tvos(14.0)); bridged over the release's own -prepareToPlay
entries.reason: read with tools/mach32_methods.py from the armv7 cache of 6.1.3 (MediaPlayer image at 0x31fe3000), MPMusicPlayerController has 64 own instance methods and 5 own class methods and -prepareToPlay is among the 64 and prepareToPlayWithCompletionHandler: is not among them; all 41 of the image's categories were read WITH THE CLASS EACH ONE EXTENDS, resolved through each category's own class pointer, and none extends MPMusicPlayerController, so nothing here can clobber a release accessor and nothing in the release clobbers this one; -aSelectorNoFrameworkHas is absent as the control. The release's whole-cache selector list (selectors_armv7.txt, 113981 DISTINCT names, a list of names and not per-class counts) reads 0 for this selector, which is absence from the WHOLE release - no class anywhere in 6.1.3 declares it AND IT HAS SOMETHING TO DO, which the other four rows here do not: the release's own -prepareToPlay is called, through objc_msgSend with sel_registerName("prepareToPlay"), because that selector lives in the device's runtime table rather than in any header this port compiles against and ARC forbids sending through a typed pointer whose type is not the method's own - the idiom MPRemoteCommandCenter71.m already uses in this family
entries.effect: the release's -prepareToPlay runs, then the completion handler is called once with nil, which is Apple's own spelling of success for `NSError *_Nullable`. The release's method returns void, so it reports no failure and none is invented. THE LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: on a queue the release fails to prepare this answers nil where Apple's would answer an error, and there is no public way to learn that on this release - synthesising one from -playbackState would be inventing a failure Apple's own accessor never reports
